title: Multi-signal Endpoint PRD and Launch Runbook (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Purpose: Define the behavioral contract, acceptance criteria, and launch runbook for a consolidated hosted API surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank in a single multi-signal endpoint. Goal is to minimize integration burden for customers that need combined workflows (e.g., embed->retrieve->rerank->generate) while ensuring predictable semantics, backward compatibility for existing endpoints, and clear operational fallbacks.
scope:
- Deliver a single API surface (multi-signal endpoint) that accepts batched requests with optional signal sections for chat, completion, embedding, and rerank.
- Behavioral contracts for ordering, determinism, timeouts, and error semantics across signal types.
- SDK surface updates (python/js) with helper builders and examples.
- Acceptance tests, load testing, and rollout plan.
- Console: per-route telemetry and error breakdown for multi-signal requests.
out_of_scope:
- Deep model architecture changes or new model support beyond curated open model catalog.
- Private deployment packaging (this is hosted-first; Dedicated follow-up project).
- New billing model design (uses existing per-token + embedding charge model).
acceptance_criteria: API accepts a single JSON payload containing optional sections: chat, completion, embeddings, rerank and returns a consolidated response with per-signal status and a top-level request status.
For requests including embeddings followed by rerank, the platform must guarantee stable ordering between embeddings and subsequent rerank calls for deterministic evaluation (within same request).
Default per-signal timeouts applied with clear override semantics; if any required signal times out, the request returns partial content with 207 Multi-Status and a consistent error schema.

Backward compatibility: existing chat/completions/embeddings/rerank single-signal endpoints remain unchanged and maintain current SLA/contract. SDKs preserve old method names and provide migration helpers.
Integrated SAMPLER and safety guardrail runs for generation signals; flagged outputs produce standard moderation error codes and telemetry events.

Automated integration tests cover 95th percentile latency under representative traffic profiles for small (1k qps), medium (10k qps), and spike (burst x5) with no request-level SLA regressions compared to baseline.
Console telemetry shows token-level cost estimates per signal, error breakdowns, and a per-route throughput/latency curve for the new endpoint.
Documentation and at least three reference recipes (embed+rerank+generate retrieval example, multi-turn chat+rerank, batch embeddings+index) available in public docs before GA.
Support runbook and escalation matrix published, support and solutions engineers trained in two enablement sessions before GA.
Security review completed and any required mitigations implemented (KMS usage validated for stored embeddings when customer opts in).
decisions: Expose multi-signal in a single endpoint instead of multiple chained calls to reduce network overhead and make atomic semantics clearer.
Return 207 Multi-Status on partial success to allow consumers to receive successful signals while being explicitly notified of failures within the same request.
Keep billing unchanged: token/embedding unit billing applied per inner signal to preserve predictable unit economics for customers.
Determinism guarantee limited to within-request ordering; no cross-request deterministic guarantees due to runtime recombination and cache eviction behavior.
risks: Increased request complexity may cause customer integration errors—mitigate with clear SDK builders and examples.
Higher memory/KV pressure when combining signals in a single request could impact tail latency—need runtime isolation knobs and improved autoscaling rules.
Ambiguity around partial responses could lead to misinterpretation in customer apps; standardized 207 response and explicit per-signal status required.
Security: embeddings stored at rest for rerank steps could pose compliance concerns; must ensure opt-in and proper KMS controls.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal + 5 beta customers receive opt-in access with detailed logging enabled; run for 2 weeks with daily checks. Phase 1 (wider beta): expand to 50 customers, add SDK helpers in minor release, monitor for customer integration issues for 4 weeks. Phase 2 (GA): enable by default for new tenants and provide migration guide for existing single-signal users; announce deprecation plan for none (we keep single-signal forever). Canary rollout uses feature flag multiSignal.v1 routed through canary dimensions: customer_tier, region, and traffic_percentage.
